messages.text: This page is a translation of the English reference. If the two differ, {english} prevails.
Not affiliated with the Government of Morocco

TheMoroccoAI.com is an independently developed digital asset owned and operated by Sohadot. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated on behalf of any government, public institution, or third-party organization or company. References to external organizations, initiatives and sources do not imply their endorsement of or participation in the project.
How TheMoroccoAI's evidence registry admits, classifies and corrects claims, what it does not establish, and a changelog tied to its public repository.
What the registry documents, what it does not establish, how evidence is admitted, and how claims are corrected. The rules below are enforced by the validator and tests that run on every change.
{independent} {statement} No institution has adopted or designated it as an official reference.

This is a privately governed research resource, not an official registry. Source attribution is not a claim of institutional partnership or endorsement. Evidence classifications, limitations and corrections are documented below. English is the authoritative editorial language; other language editions are planned and are not represented as complete.

Version {version}, sources checked {date}: {records} evidence records, {entities} entities and {relationships} typed relationships. Entity types: {types}. Each record carries the source URL, a verbatim excerpt, the publication and retrieval dates, and one classification:
Sources by type: {sources}. Primary sources are preferred; secondary press may support only an announced plan or an unverified claim.
{term} The registry covers what it has documented so far. An absent organisation, project or sector is a gap in coverage, not evidence of absence in Morocco.
{term} Public availability is not adoption. No usage, accuracy, performance or impact figure is recorded as fact.
{term} Official targets and announced plans are shown as such, never as outcomes.
{term} An operational stage rests on its latest evidence; operation after that date is not reconfirmed.
{term} A matching name does not make two organisations the same legal entity; such links are labelled as associations.
{term} Records quote public sources; they are not official statements, and the registry speaks for no institution.
A record is added only after the original source has been retrieved and the excerpt matched against it.

A lifecycle stage beyond "announced" needs a verified record that declares that stage. A signature, announcement, procurement notice, market clearance or official gazette text never establishes operation: a gazette text shows legal establishment, not activity.
An operational or pilot claim states its basis (public availability, an operator's report of use, or an independent source) and names the operator separately from any developer or provider.
Inferences drawn by the registry are labelled independent analysis and need at least two records.
Candidates that do not meet these rules are not published.
Statements the registry could not check are kept only as unverified claims, with a note saying what was not checked.
Where sources conflict or are insufficient, the stage is "unresolved", with the reason stated.
A record whose quotation still matches its source but whose claim later evidence contradicts is marked superseded and can no longer set a stage. It stays visible.

Questions the evidence cannot yet answer are published in the {gap_register}, with what is established, what is not and what would resolve them. A gap must be re-assessed whenever a new record concerns it.
When the latest evidence for an operational claim is more than 12 months old, the {questions_page} says current operation has not been reconfirmed. Elapsed time never changes a stage by itself.

Corrections are made in the data, re-validated and published as a new commit on the {repository}, so every change is visible in its history. The record's verification note says what changed and why. Corrections with a source can be sent to {contact}.

The data is published as {evidence_json} and {ontology_json}, with the gap register and derived files; {data_guide} explains how to read and verify them. No content or data licence has been declared yet; that is the owner's decision.
Breaking changes to the data contract
Independent, evidence-backed registry of Morocco's AI ecosystem: institutions, initiatives and projects tied to primary sources, with facts, targets and plans labelled separately.

Primary-source evidence records and an ontology of institutions, initiatives and projects in Morocco's AI ecosystem, with claims classified as verified fact, official target, announced plan, independent analysis or unverified claim.
Institutions, initiatives and projects in Morocco’s artificial intelligence ecosystem. Every entry cites its source, whose type is labelled, with a verbatim excerpt and dates, and {emphasis}.
facts, official targets, announced plans and our own analysis are labelled separately

{independent} TheMoroccoAI is an independent reference project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by the Government of Morocco or any institution listed here. Records quote public sources and link to them; they are not official statements.

{questions} lists which organisations have documented AI activity, which projects are operational or only announced, which models and datasets are public, and which relationships are verified. Each answer links to its evidence.
The {matrix} shows which organisations are documented as connected to which projects and initiatives, and on what evidence. The {gaps} lists what the registry cannot yet establish.

The fullest chain in this version runs from {ai2030} to the announced {jazari_network}, its planned core institute {jazari_root} and the {jazari_x0} convention signed in Fès. It then goes on to the signatories, the stated technologies and the targeted sectors. Each page shows the source excerpt, the publication and retrieval dates, and the classification of every claim.
Counts cover evidence records, plus relationships for independent analysis. An official target is never shown as an outcome. A record marked “partial” states what could not be checked.
No record has been verified for this domain yet. It stays empty rather than holding unsourced entries.
{data_guide} describes the files, identifiers, null values and versions, says which answers can be recomputed, and links to an example that checks the data independently.
{state}: what the registry currently records (classifications, documented lifecycle stages, official target records and open gaps), generated from {file}.
{file}: the list of published JSON files, with the SHA-256 of each in this version.
{file}: every evidence record, with its source URL, dates, verbatim excerpts, classification and verification status.
{file}: entity types, domains, predicates, entities and typed relationships, each citing its evidence.

Each record was retrieved from its source on the stated retrieval date, and its excerpt was matched against the retrieved text. An automated validator checks every build. It requires unique identifiers, https source URLs, valid dates and complete fields, and that every entity and relationship cites existing evidence. It also blocks forward-looking wording in records classified as fact, and rejects any relationship whose classification its evidence does not support.
The registry is deliberately selective: it omits facts it could not verify against an original source, and an absent entry is a gap in coverage. Corrections can be sent to {contact}.
